faq.q: What is the maximum investment in SCSS?
faq.a: Currently, an individual can invest up to ₹30 lakhs in the Senior Citizen's Savings Scheme.
Yes, the interest earned from the Post Office Monthly Income Scheme (POMIS) is fully taxable as per your income tax slab.

Withdrawals from an SWP are treated as capital gains. The tax depends on the holding period and the type of fund (equity-oriented or debt-oriented). Long-term capital gains from equity funds (held over 1 year) are taxed at 10% on gains above ₹1 lakh in a financial year.

faq.q: Can NRIs invest in these schemes?
faq.a: NRIs are generally not eligible to invest in schemes like SCSS, POMIS, or PMVVY. However, they can continue existing accounts if they were opened as residents. NRIs can invest in Indian mutual funds.

faq.q: What is a sustainable SWP withdrawal rate?
faq.a: A commonly suggested sustainable withdrawal rate from a diversified portfolio is around 4-6% annually, depending on market conditions and the fund's performance. A lower rate offers more safety for corpus longevity.

faq.q: How often should I review my retirement portfolio?
faq.a: It is advisable to review your retirement portfolio at least once a year, or whenever there are significant changes in your financial situation, health, or market conditions.
